title: Scientists identify the rare meteorite that killed the dinosaurs 66 million years ago
hook: The asteroid that ended the dinosaurs' long reign turns out to be an exceptionally rare type of space rock — and its chemistry rewrites how it actually killed them.
key_points: The dinosaur-killing asteroid was likely an exceptionally rare CO chondrite, from a distant part of the solar system.
Its unusual chemistry points to planet-cooling dust and debris as the deadliest factor.
That shifts blame away from sulfur inside the asteroid, the previous leading suspect.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago was likely an exceptionally rare type of meteorite called a CO chondrite, originating from a distant region of the solar system.
extra_html: Its unusual chemistry suggests that planet-cooling dust and debris thrown into the atmosphere, rather than sulfur locked inside the asteroid, delivered the deadliest blow — reshaping how scientists think the impact triggered a global die-off.

related.title: A Wobbling, Peanut-Shaped Asteroid Reshaped by Sunlight
related.hook: NASA's Lucy found that asteroid Donaldjohanson is a peanut-shaped relic of an ancient collision — slowly reshaped by sunlight, and still carrying traces of old water.
